content: The Stennis Foundation is a registered nonprofit organization under section 501(c)(3) of the IRS code. Its primary function is to raise funds and allocate them to various research projects. Currently, the foundation supports research initiatives at Duke University, the Kennedy Krieger Institute, and the San Raffaele Institute in Milan, Italy. The Stennis Foundation is dedicated to combating and ultimately eradicating the group of progressive and devastating disorders known as the Leukodystrophies. In addition to being a nationwide organization, the Stennis Foundation is a registered charity in the states of Texas, Tennessee, New Jersey, Massachusetts, and Michigan, where it has been officially recognized and granted credibility. Donations can be made through their website using PayPal or sent directly to The Stennis Foundation at P.O. Box 30065, Amarillo, TX 79120. According to their website, the Stennis Foundation is committed to raising public awareness about Leukodystrophies and generating funds to support research into these diseases. Their goal is to significantly advance research efforts by ensuring proper funding. The foundation’s mission statement is “One Step Closer to a Cure.” The origins of the foundation were inspired by Dr. Sam Stennis, a former optometrist from Amarillo, Texas. At the age of 47, Dr. Stennis was diagnosed with adult-onset Metachromatic Leukodystrophy, a rare and debilitating genetic disorder.
